summary: This week highlighted a severe squeeze on Asian supply chains, driven by escalating Red Sea shipping disruptions and volatile crude prices that pushed up bunker surcharges alongside aggressive US threats of 100% tariffs over Russian energy imports. In response, both India and China are accelerating efforts to insulate their logistics networks through major structural upgrades—like China's Pinglu Canal and India's Dedicated Freight Corridors—and expanded non-dollar settlement mechanisms. Moving forward, ocean carriers and exporters face sustained cost inflation and longer transit loops, forcing trade operators to prioritize contingency re-routing and supply chain diversification to mitigate growing geopolitical risk.
